summary: On node1, built an LVM logical volume (data_vg/data_lv) mounted at /srv/data using two loop-backed PVs (root disk had no spare partition), initially sized ~956M, then grew it live to 2.49G via vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs while it stayed mounted and its test file remained intact. Set up a systemd oneshot unit (data-lv-loop-setup.service) plus an fstab entry with x-systemd.requires so the loop devices, VG activation, and mount are fully reconstructed at boot. Restarted node1 twice via `systemctl reboot`: the first reboot exposed a systemd ordering cycle (fixed by removing local-fs.target Requires/dependency loop and switching to DefaultDependencies=no/Before=local-fs.target), and the second reboot verified the fix — boot ID changed, and /srv/data came back mounted at 2.5G with matching data checksum and no failed units, with no manual intervention.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk layout and found no free space on the sole disk (vda)
Created two loopback-backed files (1G, 1.5G) as PVs since no spare partition existed
Created VG data_vg, LV data_lv, xfs filesystem, mounted at /srv/data, wrote test file
Extended VG with second loop device, grew LV to 2.49G and xfs_growfs while mounted, verified data intact
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, lvs/vgs, df, md5sum of test file
Created and enabled systemd unit to reattach loop devices and activate VG at boot; added matching /etc/fstab entry
Rebooted node1 via systemd-run scheduled systemctl reboot; polled until reachable again
Found and fixed a systemd ordering cycle preventing boot-time activation (removed conflicting local-fs.target Requires, switched to DefaultDependencies=no)
Manually verified recovery after first reboot, then rebooted node1 a second time to prove the fix works unattended at real boot time
Verified post-second-reboot: LV active, VG has both PVs, /srv/data mounted at 2.5G, test file content and md5sum unchanged, no failed systemd units

evidence.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.xfs/mount produced /srv/data on data_vg/data_lv (~956M) with a test file written

evidence.requirement: LV grown to at least 2GB while mounted, contents intact
evidence.summary: vgextend+lvextend+xfs_growfs resized to 2.49G live; mount stayed active throughout and testfile.txt content was re-read successfully afterward
Captured boot_id 67f3a44b..., uptime, lvs/vgs showing 2 PVs healthy, df 2.5G mount, md5sum of test file, and enabled persistence service
systemd-run scheduled systemctl reboot and returned immediately with the timer/service unit names

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving restart (1st reboot)
evidence.summary: Polled boot_id (still 67f3a44b...), then connection timed out during reboot, then new boot_id 47ea332d... with fresh uptime confirmed restart

evidence.requirement: Diagnosed and fixed boot-time recovery failure after 1st reboot
evidence.summary: First reboot showed VG/mount missing due to a systemd ordering cycle; fixed unit dependencies, manually reactivated and confirmed data intact, then verified no ordering cycle/failed units remained

evidence.requirement: Second restart used to prove unattended boot-time recovery
evidence.summary: Scheduled second reboot, polled through disconnection, observed new boot_id 52e383fa... with fresh uptime confirming a genuine second restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: LV, mount, data, cluster/service health
evidence.summary: After the fixed second reboot, /srv/data auto-mounted at 2.5G, data_vg showed both PVs active, test file md5sum matched baseline exactly, persistence service active, and no failed systemd units
